page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor utilizing the arm64 architecture, operating at a frequency of 3.0 GHz. The server features 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 1843 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and software compilation via Clang scoring in the top 25%. Redis SET operations also demonstrate high throughput at 61.96 million operations per second. Single-core performance is comparatively moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier, while large-scale LLM prompt processing shows limitations on the 70B model.

From a resource density perspective, the D48pds_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that benefit from dedicated physical ARM cores and local SSD storage without the overhead of hyperthreading. It is highly suitable for multi-threaded software compilation, Redis caching layers, database operations, and general-purpose web serving. However, it is less optimal for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or advanced vector instructions like AVX.
description: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the DPDSv5 family, powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, 192.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 1843 GB local SSD. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers strong multi-core performance, particularly in software compilation and Redis SET operations, which rank in the top 25% of benchmarks. Conversely, single-core performance and text processing are weaker, falling into the bottom 25%. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and local SSD storage make it a cost-efficient choice for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, and caching layers. It is well-suited for web serving, Redis deployments, and parallel development pipelines, though it lacks support for AVX and AMX instruction sets.
